key_concepts: Genetics is the study of heredity and gene transmission
Heredity is the transfer of traits from parents to offspring
Gregor Mendel used garden peas (Pisum sativum) for inheritance experiments
Pure-breeding plants are produced by repeated self-pollination
P1, F1, and F2 generations represent parents, first filial, and second filial offspring
A monohybrid cross involves a single contrasting trait
Dominant traits mask recessive traits in heterozygous individuals
Mendel's F2 monohybrid crosses showed about a 3:1 dominant-to-recessive ratio
Genotype is the genetic makeup; phenotype is the observable trait
Homozygous individuals have identical alleles; heterozygous individuals have dissimilar al
Alleles are variant forms of a gene at the same chromosome locus
Diploid organisms have two alleles per genetic locus, one from each parent
